statement: A cafe bakes 15 cakes every day and uses 4 eggs in each cake. Eggs come in boxes of 6. How many boxes of eggs does the cafe use in one week?

choices.misconception: I worked out the number of boxes for one day and forgot to multiply by the seven days.
I found the number of eggs used in the week and forgot to change it into boxes.
I counted only the five weekdays instead of all seven days of the week.
I multiplied by 6 for the boxes instead of dividing by 6.

hints: How many eggs does one day need?
Break it into steps: eggs per day, then eggs per week, then boxes. Write the unit after each step, so that you divide by the box size at the right moment and do not stop early.
One day uses 15 x 4 = 60 eggs, which is 10 boxes.

solutions.reliable: Each day uses 15 x 4 = 60 eggs, which is 60 / 6 = 10 boxes. Over 7 days that is 7 x 10 = 70 boxes. The transferable idea: label the unit after each step (eggs per day, eggs per week, boxes) so you never stop one step short.

whyOnTest: Multi-step word problems reward tracking units; each wrong choice stops at, skips or reverses one of the three steps.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
